item.title: Version 0.0.30
item.description:
### Fixes a crash on launch that affected every machine but the developer's
ClaudeBar shipped without the bundle holding its interface text. Every label in the app is loaded from it, so the app trapped and quit the instant it drew anything — no menu bar icon, no window, no error. On the machine the releases were built from it kept working, because older build tooling wrote an absolute path to the build directory into the binary as a fallback, and that directory was right there. Nobody else had it.
0.0.29's packaging fixes were real but could not help on their own: the app got past Gatekeeper and then crashed a moment later. Releases are now smoke tested by launching the built app from outside the build directory and requiring it to survive, which is the check that would have caught this.

item.title: Version 0.0.29
item.description:
### The app now launches for everyone
Builds through 0.0.28 were missing a bundle type declaration, so macOS did not recognize ClaudeBar as an application and quietly refused to launch it whenever the copy carried a quarantine flag — which is every copy downloaded from the releases page. Nothing appeared, and because ClaudeBar has no Dock icon or window, there was nothing to indicate why. Fixed.
Builds are also universal again: 0.0.28 shipped Apple Silicon only and could not run on Intel Macs at all.
If a previous download never started for you, replace it with this build — a copy that never launched could not update itself.

item.title: Version 0.0.28
item.description:
### "100%" no longer wraps in the menu bar
At exactly 100% usage the menu bar label broke onto two lines, showing a clipped "100" stacked over "%". The item is now measured the way the system lays the text out, so a full bar reads as one line.

item.title: Version 0.0.27
item.description:
### Readable percentage on the 5-hour bar
The yellow band of the 5-hour usage bar was bright enough that the white percentage sitting on it was hard to read. It's now a deeper gold.

item.title: Version 0.0.26
item.description:
### Update dialog no longer hides
The Sparkle "Software Update" window used to open behind other windows — clicking **Check for Updates** looked like it did nothing. ClaudeBar now brings itself forward before showing update UI, for both manual and scheduled checks.

item.title: Version 0.0.25
item.description:
### Multiple accounts
Sign in to more than one Claude.ai account and switch between them:
- **Account switcher** in the popover header — click your email to change the active account. - **Settings** lists every signed-in account with a per-account Remove button. - Existing sign-ins migrate automatically; no action needed.
### Menu bar polish
- The status item is narrower and the label is centered. - The panel no longer shifts or resizes while switching accounts or when the percentage changes width.

item.title: Version 0.0.23
item.description:
### Notarized builds
ClaudeBar is now signed with an Apple Developer ID certificate and notarized by Apple. macOS no longer shows a Gatekeeper warning on first launch.
No action needed — this update installs like any other.

item.title: Version 0.0.22
item.description:
## What's new in v0.0.22
**Fixes a silent failure when connecting your session key**
If your Claude.ai account exposes more than one organization but only one of them is a paid/trackable plan (a very common setup — a personal org alongside your paid workspace), pasting your `sessionKey` and hitting Connect did nothing: no usage, no organization picker, no error. ClaudeBar now connects the single paid organization automatically in that case, shows a picker whenever there's a real choice, and surfaces a clear message when an account has no organizations at all — so connecting never dead-ends silently again.

item.title: Version 0.0.21
item.description:
## What's new in v0.0.21
**Per-model weekly limits keep working after the API change**
Claude.ai moved the per-model weekly limit out of the old `seven_day_*` windows (now empty) and into a new structure that names the model directly — currently "Fable". ClaudeBar now reads that format, so the model's weekly usage reappears in the 7-Day Windows section, labeled with the exact model name the API reports and future-proof against further model renames.

item.title: Version 0.0.20
item.description:
## What's new in v0.0.20
**Clearer label for usage-credit pools**
Dollar-denominated credit pools in the 7-Day Windows section now show as "Usage Credits" (with their $used / $limit balance) instead of an internal codename like "Amber Ladder". The label is driven by the pool's structure, so it stays correct regardless of which codename the API reports.

item.title: Version 0.0.19
item.description:
## What's new in v0.0.19
**Check for Updates button in Settings**
You can now trigger a manual update check directly from the Settings panel — no need to wait for the daily background check. The button appears under Launch at Login and invokes Sparkle immediately.

item.title: Version 0.0.18
item.description:
## What's new in v0.0.18
**7-Day windows now track the live API**
The popover's 7-Day section used to hard-code Sonnet/Opus/Design rows. When Claude.ai stopped reporting those windows, they showed a misleading **0%** instead of disappearing.
- Per-model windows now render **only when the API actually reports them** — a missing window means "not provisioned", so the row is hidden rather than shown as empty. - Any new window Claude.ai returns is surfaced automatically (no app update needed), including codenamed credit pools like `amber_ladder`, shown with their dollar balance (e.g. **$0 / $2,500**). - Known windows keep friendly names (Sonnet, Opus, Design); unrecognized codenames are humanized (`amber_ladder` → "Amber Ladder").

item.title: Version 0.0.17
item.description:
## What's new in v0.0.17
**Cask renamed: `claudebar-menubar`**
brew install --cask chiliec/tap/claudebar-menubar
The short name `claudebar` in the central Homebrew tap belongs to an unrelated project. Using a unique short name avoids `brew upgrade` silently replacing your install with the wrong app.
If you installed an earlier `chiliec/tap/claudebar`, uninstall it first:
brew uninstall --cask claudebar --force brew install --cask chiliec/tap/claudebar-menubar

item.title: Version 0.0.16
item.description:
## What's new in v0.0.16
**Homebrew Cask install + in-app Sparkle 2 updates**
brew install --cask chiliec/tap/claudebar
First launch needs no manual `xattr` or right-click bypass — the cask strips quarantine on install, and updates ship via Sparkle inside the app.
**Fixes since v0.0.15 (retracted: dyld couldn't find bundled Sparkle.framework)** - Inject `@executable_path/../Frameworks` rpath so the binary finds bundled Sparkle.framework at runtime
**Manual install (no Homebrew)**
Download the `.zip` below, unzip, drag `ClaudeBar.app` to `/Applications`. You'll see a one-time Gatekeeper prompt — right-click → Open to bypass it.
